rules.name: Behavior-specific oracle
rules.blocking: The asserted outcome can be satisfied when the behavior claimed by the test or originating requirement is broken. Trace setup, action, and oracle, and demonstrate the false-pass path.
rules.exception: Do not demand unrelated behavior outside the requirement. Assertions inside called helpers count. A failed soft assertion still fails a Playwright test.

rules.name: Required setup and validation remain mandatory
rules.blocking: An introduced catch, early return, conditional, or runtime skip permits required setup or validation to be bypassed without failing the test.
rules.exception: Optional UI handling is legitimate when the required outcome is still asserted. Moving a conditional into a page object does not itself repair a false pass.

rules.name: Identity, environment, and data-source fidelity
rules.blocking: The changed flow uses a different actor, org, environment, or data source than its contract, and the oracle cannot distinguish that substitution.
rules.exception: A local run or --no-deps flag alone does not prove CI failure. Establish the configured path and mismatch.

rules.name: Retry safety and honest stability
rules.blocking: A retry can repeat a completed mutation, invert a toggle, or bypass a failed prerequisite so that the test accepts an incorrect result.
rules.exception: Bounded retries of idempotent readiness actions are valid. Increased timeout or retry count is a review signal, not automatic proof of masking. Keep first-attempt and retry-recovered results distinct.

rules.name: Isolation and partial-setup cleanup
rules.blocking: A changed lifecycle leaks shared state, breaks independent execution, or loses the identity needed to clean up a resource after partially completed setup.
rules.exception: Demonstrate the lifecycle and affected state. Fixed expected counts are valid when setup controls the dataset.

rules.name: Cumulative integration and caller compatibility
rules.blocking: The cumulative PR change breaks a reachable caller, fixture, project selection, or shared setup contract, including callers unchanged in the latest push.
rules.exception: Read both sides of the dependency and consider base behavior. Pre-existing defects unrelated to the PR are advisory, not new blockers.

rules.name: Ownership and justified abstraction
rules.blocking: A concrete violation of an explicit repository architecture contract creates incompatible duplicated behavior or places lifecycle responsibility where it cannot be enforced.
rules.exception: A new utils file, a single consumer, a loop, or similar-looking code is not sufficient evidence. Compare existing implementations and actual callers. Pure maintainability preferences are advisory.

rules.name: Reliable observation and synchronization
rules.blocking: A changed event subscription, immediate snapshot, selector, or wait can demonstrably miss the relevant state or accept an unrelated element.
rules.exception: Use the repository's co-first role/test-id guidance. Do not invent accessible names or test IDs. A fallback selector is not automatically defective.
